steps.say: I can feel the cold now. Forty years I stood between this Abbey and the cold.
We rendered them, child. The sick. The old. The ones the Drip had already started on. Tallow for the Great Wick, so the flame would not go out. I signed every page of that ledger myself.
And it was never enough. The more we fed it, the faster it guttered.
Something up there is drinking it.
Go and look at it for me. I never had the courage to climb.
The black flame on his head bends, gutters, and goes out. What is left of him settles into the floor, soft as a snuffed candle.

then.say: Aldous lowers his shield and kneels by what is left of the man he guarded for eleven years.
Rest, Father. Somebody should say it, and I'm the only one of us left who can.

steps.say: In the corner of the Nave, chains that have not moved in forty years begin to turn. Far above, something answers them.
